beats.text: Netflix offered $1 million to beat its own recommender.
beats.note: The contest began on 2 October 2006. The target was a test score of 0.8572, a 10 percent improvement on Netflix's Cinematch.
The training set held 100,480,507 ratings from 480,189 users on 17,770 films.
BellKor's Pragmatic Chaos won, announced on 18 September 2009. The Ensemble matched its test result but submitted 20 minutes later.

beats.context: FlowingData reported that the winning solution combined over 800 models from four teams.

beats.text: Netflix did not ship the winner.
beats.note: In April 2012 its engineers wrote that the extra accuracy did not seem to justify the engineering effort needed to put it into production.
Netflix said algorithms from the first year of the contest were used and remain a key part of its recommender.
On 12 March 2010 Netflix dropped it, after a lawsuit and Federal Trade Commission privacy concerns.

beats.text: Winning was not the same as shipping.
